You are implementing Task 8 of a 9-task visual redesign of a static vanilla-JS website (BusinessServices). Tasks 3-7 built css/components.css up through the portfolio/prices/about layer. Your task APPENDS the FINAL layers: contacts, focus visibility, responsive, and reduced motion. After you, the stylesheet is complete.

Working directory: c:\Users\leont\Desktop\CleaningSystem-main
Git branch: redesign/warm-premium (already checked out — commit here, do not switch branches)

READ THIS FIRST — it is your requirements, with the exact CSS to use verbatim:
.superpowers/sdd/2026-08-28-cleaning-site-redesign/task-8-brief.md

THIS IS A TRANSCRIPTION TASK. The brief's Step 1 (contacts) and Step 2 (focus, responsive, reduced motion) contain the complete, final CSS. Copy both character-for-character. Do not improve, reformat, reorder, rename, or "fix" any value.

WHAT TO DO:
APPEND the brief's Step 1 CSS block, then the brief's Step 2 CSS block, to the END of css/components.css, in that order. Do not modify, reorder, or delete anything already in the file — the layers from Tasks 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 must remain exactly as they are. Append only.

ORDERING MATTERS — DO NOT REORDER. These blocks must land in the brief's order and at the END of the file:
- The `@media (max-width: 900px)` and `@media (max-width: 640px)` blocks must come AFTER every base rule they override. Hoisting them earlier silently disables the responsive layout.
- The `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block must be LAST. It uses `!important` on animation/transition duration — that is the ONE place `!important` is permitted in this file, and it is required for the accessibility override to win. Copy it exactly. Do not add `!important` anywhere else.

CONTEXT FROM EARLIER TASKS that the brief cannot know:
- All custom properties you reference are already defined in the :root block at the top of the file. Do not redefine any of them.
- `#form-status` had its inline style stripped in Task 2, so this layer's `#form-status` rule is what styles it. Expected.
- The old stylesheet had NO focus rules at all. The `:focus-visible` block in Step 2 is the fix — it is new behaviour, not a duplicate.
- `.form-group input:focus` (Step 1) and `.form-group input:focus-visible { outline: none }` (Step 2) coexist deliberately: the inputs get a brass ring via box-shadow rather than an outline. Both are required — do not drop either, and do not merge them.
- js/components/header.js, footer.js and serviceCard.js were DELETED in Task 2 (dead duplicates). js/components/index.js is the only component file.

GLOBAL CONSTRAINTS (bind every task; violating any fails the task):
1. No content text changes. Do not touch any .js file.
2. No structural changes. Do not touch index.html.
3. `frontend/` is a stale duplicate tree with its own css/. Do not read from it, do not write to it.
6. Token values are exact — character-for-character from the brief.

SCOPE: modify ONLY css/components.css, and only by appending. Nothing else.

ENVIRONMENT: NO node, npm, npx, or headless browser (python 3.14 only; command is `python`, NOT `python3`). Do not attempt browser verification, do not install anything, do not claim a browser check passed. The brief's Step 3 asks you to tab through the page, submit the form, and toggle OS reduce-motion — IMPOSSIBLE here. Report Step 3 as DEFERRED to the controller's final visual pass.

REQUIRED STATIC VERIFICATION (run these, paste real output into your report):
  grep -c "!important" css/components.css                → 4   (all four inside the prefers-reduced-motion block, nowhere else)
  grep -n "!important" css/components.css                → confirm every hit is inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)
  grep -c "focus-visible" css/components.css             → at least 5
  grep -c "^\.contacts-wrapper {" css/components.css     → 1
  grep -c "^\.order-form {" css/components.css           → 1
  grep -c "^\.contacts-info {" css/components.css        → 1
  grep -c "^#form-status {" css/components.css           → 1
  grep -c "prefers-reduced-motion" css/components.css    → 1
  grep -c "max-width: 900px\|max-width: 640px" css/components.css   → 2
  tail -3 css/components.css                              → must be the closing of the reduced-motion block (it is LAST in the file)
  grep -c -- "--ink:" css/components.css                 → 1   (:root not duplicated)
  grep -c "^header {" css/components.css                 → 1   (Task 4 survived)
  grep -c "^\.portfolio-card {" css/components.css       → 1   (Task 7 survived)
  awk '{o+=gsub(/{/,"{"); c+=gsub(/}/,"}")} END{print o, c}' css/components.css   → the two numbers must be EQUAL
  git status --short                                      → only css/components.css
Also confirm the file still begins with the "BusinessServices — Design System" banner and the :root block (i.e. you appended, not overwrote).

COMMIT: one commit on the current branch. Use:
  git -c user.email=leontachyan@gmail.com -c user.name=leont commit -m "style: add contacts, focus, responsive and reduced-motion layers"

REPORT: write your full report to
.superpowers/sdd/2026-08-28-cleaning-site-redesign/task-8-report.md
covering: what you appended, the verification commands with real output, what you deferred and why, and any concerns.

Then return ONLY this short contract as your final message:
- STATUS: DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | NEEDS_CONTEXT | BLOCKED
- COMMITS: <short sha(s)>
- VERIFICATION: one line summarising the static checks
- CONCERNS: one line, or "none"

You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

# Task 8 Report: Contacts, Focus Visibility, Responsive, and Reduced Motion Layers

## Summary
Successfully appended all required CSS layers to the END of `css/components.css` as specified in the brief. The stylesheet is now complete.

## What Was Appended

### Step 1: Contacts Layer (12. CONTACTS)
- `.contacts-wrapper`: Grid layout with 1.15fr/.85fr columns for form and info panels
- `.order-form`: Styled form container with brass ring focus state (box-shadow)
- `.form-group`: Flex layout for label+input groups with 6px gap
- `.form-grid-2`: Two-column grid for form fields
- Form inputs/textarea: Canvas background, border, 44px minimum height, fast transitions
- Focus state: Brass border color with 3px rgba brass halo via box-shadow
- `#form-status`: Centered text message display (inline style stripped in Task 2)
- `.contacts-info`: Dark ink background panel with light text, brass accents on dark
- `.contacts-info h3`: Playfair Display title in white on ink background

### Step 2: Focus Visibility, Responsive, and Reduced Motion Layers

#### 13. FOCUS VISIBILITY
- `:focus-visible`: Global brass outline with 2px width and 2px offset
- `header :focus-visible`, `.contacts-info :focus-visible`, `.price-card.featured :focus-visible`: Brass outline uses accent-on-ink color (lighter on dark backgrounds)
- `.form-group input:focus-visible`, `.form-group select:focus-visible`, `.form-group textarea:focus-visible`: `outline: none` (inputs get box-shadow brass ring instead)

#### 14. RESPONSIVE
- `@media (max-width: 900px)`:
  - `.features-grid`: Collapses to 1 column
  - `.contacts-wrapper`: Collapses to 1 column (form above info)
  - `.comparison-slider`: Height reduced to 340px
  
- `@media (max-width: 640px)`:
  - `.header-container`: Padding reduced to var(--s4), gap reduced to var(--s3)
  - `.page-container`: Left/right padding reduced to var(--s4), bottom padding var(--s7)
  - `.hero-stats`: Stacked vertically instead of horizontal
  - `.stat-item + .stat-item`: Horizontal divider replaced with top border
  - `.form-grid-2`: Single column layout
  - Multiple components (`.order-form`, `.contacts-info`, `.price-card`, `.modal-content`, portfolio cards): Padding reduced to var(--s5)
  - `.comparison-slider`: Height reduced to 280px
  - `.portfolio-before-after-section`: Margin-top increased to var(--s8)

#### 15. REDUCED MOTION
- `html { scroll-behavior: auto; }`: Disables smooth scrolling
- Universal selector `*, *::before, *::after`:
  - `animation-duration: .01ms !important`: Effectively disables all animations
  - `animation-iteration-count: 1 !important`: Prevents animation loops
  - `transition-duration: .01ms !important`: Effectively disables all transitions
  - `scroll-behavior: auto !important`: Override to auto scrolling
- Hover states disabled via `transform: none`:
